intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of Angkor Wat, then continue to the mysterious Bayon temple with its 216 serene stone faces and the jungle-engulfed Ta Prohm where tree roots swallow ancient ruins.

experiences.name: Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace compound and the adjacent Silver Pagoda, home to a life-sized gold Buddha studded with 9,584 diamonds. Stroll the surrounding riverside promenade along the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers and explore the nearby National Museum of Cambodia for deep historical context.

experiences.name: Kep Beach and Crab Market Seafood Experience
experiences.description: Relax on the quiet, palm-fringed shores of Kep Beach, then head to the famous Crab Market to feast on freshly caught blue swimming crabs cooked in Kampot pepper sauce — a quintessential Cambodian coastal culinary tradition. Rent a kayak to explore the nearby mangroves of Kep National Park.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Street Food Night Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided evening street food tour through the bustling lanes of Phnom Penh, sampling local delicacies such as num banh chok (Khmer noodles), lok lak beef, bai sach chrouk (pork and rice), and fresh sugar cane juice. Discover hidden food stalls and learn about Cambodian culinary history and French colonial food influences.
experiences.location: BKK1 and Riverside area, Phnom Penh

experiences.name: Otres Beach Sunset Kayaking and Snorkeling
experiences.description: Spend a day at the laid-back Otres Beach, one of Cambodia's most beautiful and least crowded stretches of white sand. Join a guided sea kayaking and snorkeling excursion to nearby islands in the Gulf of Thailand, exploring coral reefs and vibrant marine life, finishing with a spectacular sunset over the water.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing and clearing customs, arrange a tuk-tuk or shared taxi to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the local neighborhood to get oriented. Visit the nearby Angkor Night Market area for a gentle introduction to Siem Reap's atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street area for a relaxed first evening. Explore the lively street scene, browse local souvenir stalls, and soak in the Siem Reap vibe. Visit the Old Market (Phsar Chas) which stays open into the evening for a taste of local commerce.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or upon arrival — try a local noodle soup (kuy teav) from a street stall near your accommodation for around $1–2.
meals.dinner: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — affordable, authentic Khmer cuisine. Try amok (fish curry in coconut) for around $4–6. Budget meal total: ~$6–8.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to Cambodian Riel at the airport or a local money changer (Cambodia widely accepts USD). Tuk-tuk from airport to Angkor area costs around $8–12. Negotiate prices upfront. November is the start of the dry season — expect pleasant, cooler weather, perfect for sightseeing.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (5:00 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise. Watch the sun rise over the main temple reflected in the lotus pond — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting Hindu epics, and the central towers. Hire a local guide at the gate for ~$20 for deeper historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom, the ancient walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, then explore the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Take a break in the shade and hydrate — the afternoon sun can be intense.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation to rest and shower. Head to the Night Market for dinner and browse handmade crafts, silk scarves, and artwork. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a local restaurant (some offer free shows with dinner).

meals.breakfast: Rice porridge (bobor) or a baguette sandwich from a local bakery near the hotel — $1–2.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or grab food from a vendor near the Angkor complex. Local fried rice or noodles at a stall: $2–3.
meals.dinner: Soria Moria Restaurant or a local restaurant near Night Market — try lok lak (stir-fried beef with rice) for $4–5. Budget: ~$5–7.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass for $62 if you plan to visit over multiple days — it offers great value. Single-day pass is $37. Start early to beat the heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a water bottle. Tuk-tuk rental for the day: ~$15–20 (negotiate a full-day rate).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm Temple, famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple,' where ancient tree roots dramatically engulf the stone ruins. Arrive early to enjoy it before tour groups arrive. Then head to Banteay Kdei, a quieter Buddhist temple with intricate carvings and a peaceful atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the outer circuit temples: Preah Khan (a sprawling temple complex with jungle overgrowth) and Neak Pean (an artificial island temple surrounded by water — particularly scenic in November when water levels are high). These are less crowded and offer a more adventurous experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop (free entry) near the Grand Circuit to watch skilled artisans create traditional Khmer silk, stone carvings, and lacquerware. Browse their ethical shop for quality souvenirs. End the evening with a traditional Khmer cooking class if budget allows (~$15–25).

meals.breakfast: Num banh chok (Khmer noodles with green curry) from a local market stall — $1–1.50.
meals.lunch: Roadside stall near Preah Khan — grilled skewers, rice, and fresh coconut water for $3–4.
meals.dinner: Haven Restaurant (social enterprise training vulnerable youth) — excellent Khmer cuisine for $5–8. Highly recommended for budget and ethics.

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm is very popular — arrive before 8:00 AM for the best experience. Wear comfortable, closed-toe shoes as temple floors can be uneven. Bring your Angkor Pass. The outer circuit temples require more travel time — a tuk-tuk for the day is essential (~$15).

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Banteay Srei, located about 25 km north of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is dedicated to Shiva and is renowned for its extraordinarily detailed pink sandstone carvings — considered the jewel of Khmer art. The smaller scale makes it feel intimate and special.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return journey, stop at the Landmine Museum (founded by former child soldier Aki Ra) — a powerful and educational experience about Cambodia's tragic history with landmines. Entry is a small donation (~$5). Then visit Banteay Samré, another well-preserved but rarely visited temple nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Siem Reap, explore the vibrant Kandal Village area — a hip neighborhood with indie cafes, boutique shops, and local art galleries. Enjoy a relaxing evening browsing and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: French baguette with pâté or eggs at a local café — $2–3 (French colonial influence is strong in Cambodia).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab food near Banteay Srei from roadside vendors — spring rolls and fruit for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Marum Restaurant (another social enterprise) — innovative Khmer-fusion dishes for $5–8. Try the amok or stuffed lemongrass skewers.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a separate tuk-tuk trip — negotiate a half-day rate of ~$15–20 including return. The Landmine Museum is a sobering but essential visit for understanding modern Cambodian history. Your Angkor Pass covers Banteay Srei and Banteay Samré.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip on Tonle Sap Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Visit a floating village (Kampong Phluk is recommended over the more touristy Chong Kneas) to see how thousands of Cambodians live on the water. The stilted houses and floating schools are fascinating. Best visited in November when water levels are still high.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Siem Reap War Museum (entry ~$5) for a comprehensive look at Cambodia's military history, including Khmer Rouge weapons and vehicles. Then explore the Angkor National Museum ($12 entry) for context on the Khmer Empire's history and art — worth the splurge for history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Khmer massage on Pub Street — budget options start at $6–8 for an hour. Then browse the Night Market one more time for any last-minute Siem Reap souvenirs before preparing to move on.

meals.breakfast: Coconut pancakes and fresh tropical fruit from a morning market stall — $1.50–2.
meals.lunch: Fresh fish from the lake area near Kampong Phluk — local family restaurants serve simple but delicious fish dishes for $3–4.
meals.dinner: Street food along Pub Street — try a variety of skewers, spring rolls, and mango sticky rice for $4–6 total.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kampong Phluk boat trip through your guesthouse or a local operator for $15–20 per person. Avoid the overly commercialized Chong Kneas village. The Angkor National Museum is optional based on budget — if you've done thorough temple exploration, you may skip it. Pack insect repellent for the lake visit.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (Cambodia's capital). Giant Ibis or Mekong Express buses are comfortable and cost $9–15. The journey takes approximately 5–6 hours. Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a budget guesthouse near the riverside (Riverside area or BKK1 neighborhood). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning royal complex with its gleaming spires is a must-see. Entry is $10 and includes both sites.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Phnom Penh Riverside Promenade (Sisowath Quay) as the sun sets over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. The waterfront comes alive in the evening with locals exercising, street food vendors, and a festive atmosphere. Browse the night food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast before the bus departs — banh mi (Cambodian baguette sandwich) for $1–2 from a Siem Reap street vendor.
meals.lunch: Lunch stop on the bus route or at a roadside restaurant — rice with grilled pork (bai sach chrouk) for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant or street stalls along Sisowath Quay — try kuy teav (noodle soup) or beef lok lak for $4–6.

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket in advance through your guesthouse or online (Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and reliability). Phnom Penh budget guesthouses near the riverside cost $8–15/night. Keep valuables secure — bag snatching from motorbikes has been reported along the riverside, especially at night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison where an estimated 17,000 people were tortured and killed. This is a deeply moving and historically essential experience. Entry is $5; audio guides are available for $3. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from city center, $3–4 by tuk-tuk). This is the most significant of the Khmer Rouge extermination sites. The audio guide ($6) is exceptional and deeply humanizing. A memorial stupa contains the skulls and bones of victims. This is a sobering but profoundly important visit.
day_by_day.evening: After a heavy day of history, decompress with a walk through the Phnom Penh Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — an art deco yellow dome building selling everything from jewelry to street food. Then enjoy a quiet dinner and reflect on the day's experiences.

meals.breakfast: Bai sach chrouk (rice and grilled pork) — Phnom Penh's signature breakfast dish, available at morning markets for $1.50–2.
meals.lunch: Simple lunch near Tuol Sleng — local noodle shop or rice dish for $2–3. Eat light given the emotional weight of the day.
meals.dinner: Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a renowned social enterprise training street youth in hospitality. Tapas-style Khmer dishes for $5–8. Book ahead if possible.

day_by_day.notes: This is an emotionally demanding day — be prepared for a powerful and sobering experience. The Khmer Rouge genocide (1975–1979) killed an estimated 1.7–2.5 million Cambodians. Dress respectfully (covered shoulders and knees). Photography is permitted but be mindful and respectful. Take your time and don't rush through either site.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia near the Royal Palace — a beautiful terracotta building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture. Entry is $10. Spend 1.5–2 hours among the stunning Angkor-era statues and artifacts. Then visit Wat Phnom, the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name, for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel day to the coast: Take a bus or minivan from Phnom Penh to Kampot (~3–4 hours, $6–9 via Mekong Express or Capitol Bus). Kampot is a charming riverside colonial town that serves as a gateway to the beaches of southern Cambodia. Check into a budget guesthouse ($8–15/night).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kampot's charming French colonial old town on foot. Stroll along the riverside promenade, admire the colonial architecture, and visit the old market. Enjoy the relaxed, slow-paced atmosphere that makes Kampot a beloved backpacker destination.

meals.breakfast: Num pang (Cambodian sandwich) from a street vendor near your Phnom Penh guesthouse — $1–1.50.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch before or during the bus journey — roadside restaurant with rice and curry for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Rusty Keyhole or Epic Arts Café in Kampot — budget-friendly Western and Khmer fusion dishes for $4–7. Try the Kampot pepper crab if budget allows (Kampot is world-famous for its pepper).

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is known for its Kampot pepper — one of the world's finest. Look for it at local markets as an excellent and affordable souvenir. The riverside town has a very laid-back vibe — perfect for decompressing after the intense Phnom Penh history days. Book bus tickets in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle or motorbike ($5–10/day) and explore the Kampot countryside. Visit a working Kampot pepper farm for a free or low-cost tour — learn about the cultivation of this prized spice. Then cycle to the nearby salt fields and Teuk Chhou rapids for scenic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short trip (~30 minutes by tuk-tuk or motorbike) to Kep, a former French colonial beach resort. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market and enjoy freshly cooked blue crab with Kampot pepper sauce — one of Cambodia's signature dishes. Swim at Kep Beach (small but pleasant) or the nearby Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) for pristine white sand and clear water ($5 boat return).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for a sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River — many guesthouses offer these for $5–8 per person, often including a drink. Watch fireflies light up the mangroves as darkness falls — a magical experience unique to Kampot.

meals.breakfast: Fruit smoothie and banana pancake at a Kampot riverside café — $2–3.
meals.lunch: Fresh blue crab with Kampot pepper at Kep Crab Market — $6–10 for a whole crab (splurge-worthy). Eat at the market stalls for the freshest and most affordable option.
meals.dinner: Baraka Restaurant in Kampot — excellent Middle Eastern and Khmer fusion for $4–7, with a lovely riverside setting.

day_by_day.notes: November is an excellent time for Kep and Kampot — the rainy season has just ended, vegetation is lush and green, and the sea is calm. Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) is a beautiful half-day trip with hammocks, simple bungalows, and crystal-clear water. Motorbike rental requires confidence — opt for a bicycle or tuk-tuk if you're not experienced.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Cambodia — take a leisurely breakfast at a Kampot riverside café and soak in the peaceful atmosphere. If time permits, visit Bokor National Park (accessible by motorbike or organized tour ~$15) for stunning mountain scenery, an abandoned French hill station, and panoramic ocean views. The drive up is spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin your journey home or to your next destination. From Kampot, take a bus or shared taxi back to Phnom Penh (~3–4 hours) for international flights, or head to Sihanoukville (~2 hours) if your flight departs from there. Use travel time to reflect on an incredible 10 days in Cambodia.
day_by_day.evening: If you have a late flight from Phnom Penh, enjoy a final Cambodian dinner near the airport or riverside. Pick up last-minute souvenirs — Kampot pepper, silk scarves, or handmade crafts make excellent gifts.

meals.breakfast: Full Cambodian breakfast at a riverside café in Kampot — rice porridge, tropical fruit, and strong Cambodian iced coffee ($2–4).
meals.lunch: Roadside stop during the bus journey — simple rice dish for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Final Cambodian meal at a Phnom Penh riverside restaurant — splurge slightly on your last night with a full amok and lok lak spread for $8–12.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary for 10 days: Accommodation ~$80–150, Transport ~$60–90, Food ~$80–120, Entrance fees ~$90–110, Activities ~$40–60. Total estimated budget: $350–530 USD for 10 days, excluding international flights. Cambodia is very affordable — you can comfortably travel on $40–55/day. Depart with memories of ancient temples, resilient people, stunning landscapes, and incredible food.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to boutique hotel in Angkor Archaeological Park area, check in, freshen up, and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Light orientation walk around the hotel neighborhood. Visit the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate for a gentle first glimpse of the ancient ruins — a short tuk-tuk ride away. Admire the iconic stone faces and the moat without entering the full complex yet.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Siem Reap town center to explore Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area. Browse local handicrafts and soak in the lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport meal)
meals.lunch: Grab a bite at the airport or a casual café near the hotel upon arrival — try Khmer Kitchen Restaurant for affordable local fare
meals.dinner: Cuisine Wat Damnak or Mahob Restaurant — mid-range Khmer fine dining experience; budget ~$12–20 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Exchange currency at a reputable money changer in town or use an ATM. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Book a reliable tuk-tuk driver for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for sunrise at Angkor Wat (enter by 5:30 AM). Watch the sun rise over the iconic five towers reflected in the lotus pond — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Hindu epics, and the central sanctuary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue inside the Angkor Archaeological Park. Visit the Bayon Temple inside Angkor Thom — famous for its 216 serene stone faces. Then explore the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest and freshen up. Enjoy a traditional Apsara dance dinner show at Angkor Village Theatre or Smile of Angkor — a cultural highlight combining Khmer classical dance with a set dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack from a street vendor near Angkor Wat gate (rice porridge/congee ~$1–2) or hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Blue Pumpkin Café near the park entrance — sandwiches, Khmer dishes, fresh juices; budget ~$6–10
meals.dinner: Apsara dinner show set menu ~$18–25 per person, inclusive of performance

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) — it offers the best value and covers all major temples. Start very early to beat the heat and crowds. Wear light, breathable clothing and bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ta Prohm — the jungle temple famously left entwined with massive tree roots, made iconic by the film Tomb Raider. Arrive early for atmospheric, crowd-free photos. Then visit Banteay Kdei, a quieter Buddhist temple nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Srah Srang (the Royal Bath) and Prasat Kravan, a small but beautifully carved 10th-century brick temple. In the late afternoon, visit Pre Rup for stunning panoramic views of the surrounding jungle from its elevated towers.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Angkor Night Market in Siem Reap town — a vibrant open-air market with local crafts, silk scarves, artwork, and street food stalls. Great for souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local rice and egg dish from a roadside stall near the park
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local vendor near Ta Prohm or eat at a nearby open-air restaurant — Fish Amok (Khmer curry) ~$5–8
meals.dinner: Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth; excellent Khmer and Western food; budget ~$10–15

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 of your Angkor Pass. Wear sturdy shoes as temple paths can be uneven. Bring insect repellent for Ta Prohm's jungle setting.

day_by_day.morning: Use your 3rd Angkor Pass day for the outlying temples. Hire a tuk-tuk for the Grand Circuit. Start with Preah Khan — a sprawling, atmospheric temple with long colonnaded corridors and towering trees. Then visit Neak Pean, a unique artificial island temple surrounded by water (November is ideal as the water levels are high).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ta Som, a small but charming temple with a famous tree-engulfed eastern gopura. Then head to the East Mebon, built on an artificial island in the East Baray reservoir. End with a visit to the massive Angkor Thom area's less-visited Phimeanakas palace complex.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel pool or spa. Treat yourself to a traditional Khmer massage in Siem Reap — many reputable mid-range spas offer 1-hour sessions for $12–18.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Local Khmer restaurant near the Grand Circuit — Lok Lak (stir-fried beef with rice) ~$4–7
meals.dinner: Viroth's Restaurant — elegant garden setting, authentic Khmer cuisine; budget ~$12–18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Final day of your 3-day Angkor Pass. The Grand Circuit is less crowded than the Small Circuit — a more peaceful experience. November weather is generally pleasant and dry, ideal for temple exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' located about 25 km north of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest in all of Angkor. Visit the nearby Banteay Samré temple on the way back.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Landmine Museum (Cambodia Landmine Museum) on the return journey — a sobering and important cultural experience highlighting Cambodia's tragic recent history and ongoing demining efforts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Artisans Angkor workshop and showroom in Siem Reap — watch skilled artisans create traditional silk, lacquerware, and stone carvings. Browse for high-quality, ethically made souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Banteay Srei village — simple Khmer set meal ~$4–6
meals.dinner: Mie Café — contemporary Cambodian cuisine in a stylish setting; budget ~$12–16 per person

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk or private car for this day trip (~$25–35 for the full day). The road to Banteay Srei is paved and in good condition. The Landmine Museum charges a small entrance fee (~$5) which supports demining operations.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus or shared minivan from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (~5–6 hours, ~$10–15 by comfortable tourist bus). Book with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for reliability. Enjoy the countryside scenery along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early afternoon. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel near the riverside (Sisowath Quay area). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and the Silver Pagoda — a stunning complex of royal buildings and sacred Buddhist shrines.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Tonle Sap and Mekong riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay). Watch the sunset over the confluence of the two rivers. Browse the vibrant Night Market along the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at hotel before departure or at the Siem Reap bus station
meals.lunch: Snack or meal on the bus, or stop at a roadside restaurant during the journey
meals.dinner: Romdeng Restaurant — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including regional specialties; budget ~$12–18

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for safety and comfort. Royal Palace entry fee ~$10. Dress modestly for the Silver Pagoda (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. A deeply moving and essential experience to understand Cambodia's recent history. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from the city center) — the most significant memorial site of the Khmer Rouge genocide. The audio guide is excellent and deeply informative. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia, housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cruise on the Mekong River — many operators offer 1–2 hour cruises departing from the riverfront (~$8–15). Then dine in the lively Riverside district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near the riverside — try a Khmer baguette (nom pang) with pâté ~$1–2
meals.lunch: Friends (The Restaurant) — another social enterprise near the National Museum; great tapas-style Cambodian food; ~$8–12
meals.dinner: Dine at a riverside restaurant on Sisowath Quay — try Malis for upscale Khmer cuisine; budget ~$15–20

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally heavy experiences — take your time and be respectful. Entry fees: Tuol Sleng ~$5, Choeung Ek ~$6. Hire a tuk-tuk for the day (~$15–20) to cover all sites comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus or shared taxi from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (~4 hours, ~$8–12). Alternatively, take a direct bus to Kampot (~3 hours, ~$7–10) — a charming riverside town that serves as a base for nearby Kep Beach. Opt for Kampot for a more authentic, relaxed experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kampot. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or riverside bungalow. Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~$3–7/day) and explore the charming French colonial town center, the old market, and the riverfront. Visit Bokor Hill Station viewpoint if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at a riverside bar or restaurant watching the Kampot River at sunset. The town has a wonderfully laid-back atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop during bus journey or arrive and eat at a local Kampot eatery — Khmer noodle soup ~$2–4
meals.dinner: Rikitikitavi Restaurant — popular riverside spot with Khmer and international food; budget ~$8–14

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is far more relaxed and authentic than Sihanoukville, which has undergone significant development. November is a great time to visit the coast as the dry season has just begun. Book accommodation in advance for weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kep — a sleepy former French colonial beach resort town 25 km from Kampot. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market on the seafront — a must-visit for fresh seafood. Walk along the coastal promenade and visit the ruins of old colonial villas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at Kep Beach or the more scenic Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a short 20-minute boat ride from Kep pier (~$5 return). Enjoy the pristine white sand beach, clear waters, and simple beach bungalows. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot by tuk-tuk or shared taxi. Visit the Kampot Pepper Farm if still open (some offer evening tours) — Kampot pepper is world-renowned. Enjoy a final evening along the river.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or local café in Kampot
meals.lunch: Fresh Kep crab with Kampot pepper sauce at the Kep Crab Market — a true culinary highlight; budget ~$8–15
meals.dinner: Ellie's Restaurant or Kampot Riverfront café — wood-fired pizza or Khmer dishes; budget ~$8–12

day_by_day.notes: Rabbit Island is best visited midweek to avoid weekend crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling. Tuk-tuk to Kep and back from Kampot costs ~$10–15 return.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Kampot — take a relaxed kayaking or boat tour along the Kampot River through mangroves (~$10–15). Visit the Kampot Pepper Plantation for a guided tour and tasting (~$5). Pick up some Kampot pepper as a souvenir.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to Phnom Penh by bus (~3 hours) for onward flights, or travel directly to Siem Reap if your departure is from there. Use the afternoon for any last-minute souvenir shopping in Phnom Penh at the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) — great for silk, handicrafts, and clothing at bargain prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Phnom Penh or at the airport. Reflect on an incredible 10 days of temples, history, culture, and beaches.

meals.breakfast: Final Kampot breakfast at your guesthouse — fresh fruit, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Quick meal at a local restaurant near the Russian Market in Phnom Penh — Bai Sach Chrouk (pork and rice) ~$2–3
meals.dinner: Khmer Surin Restaurant near the riverside for a final celebratory Khmer meal; budget ~$12–18

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transport and flight details the night before. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport check-in. Consider purchasing Kampot pepper, silk scarves, and Angkor-themed artwork as authentic Cambodian souvenirs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique stay within the Angkor Archaeological Park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private welcome orientation and check-in at your boutique property. Freshen up and enjoy a curated welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens or poolside terrace to acclimate. Late afternoon: gentle introductory tuk-tuk ride through the nearby village lanes surrounding the park to absorb the atmosphere without overexertion.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the hotel terrace with views toward the jungle canopy. Private candlelit welcome dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring refined Khmer cuisine — try amok trei (fish amok) and lok lak beef tenderloin.

meals.breakfast: N/A — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel upon check-in: fresh spring rolls, tropical fruit platter, and coconut water
meals.dinner: In-hotel signature restaurant — multi-course Khmer tasting menu with wine pairing; recommended dishes include fish amok, Khmer red curry, and mango sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH lands at 13:00. Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Keep Day 1 light to allow for jet lag recovery. Request early check-in if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private sunrise tour of Angkor Wat — arrive before 05:30 to secure a prime reflection pool position. A dedicated expert guide explains the temple's cosmological symbolism, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and Vishnu iconography. Champagne breakfast picnic served at a private spot near the western causeway post-sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the walled city of Angkor Thom: the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon pyramid temple, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Private air-conditioned vehicle with historian guide. Rest back at the hotel midday during peak heat (12:00–14:30) with pool time.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ta Prohm temple at golden hour — the 'Tomb Raider' temple where ancient silk-cotton trees embrace stone galleries. Exclusive after-hours access arranged if possible. Dinner at a premium Siem Reap restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Champagne picnic breakfast near Angkor Wat reflection pool — croissants, fresh fruit, Cambodian iced coffee, and local rice porridge (bobor)
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled tiger prawns, green papaya salad, and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Dining at Cuisine Wat Damnak or equivalent fine-dining Khmer restaurant in Siem Reap — contemporary tasting menu using seasonal Cambodian ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Wake-up call at 04:30. Bring insect repellent and a light layer for the early morning. Hire a specialized Angkor historian guide for deeper cultural context.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer Angkor circuit: Preah Khan temple (City of the Sacred Sword) — a vast monastic complex with towering fig trees and atmospheric corridors. Then Neak Pean, an artificial island temple set in a pond, accessible by a raised wooden walkway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit East Mebon and Pre Rup temples — stunning laterite pyramid temples from the 10th century. Pre Rup's upper terrace offers panoramic views over the jungle canopy, especially beautiful in the late afternoon light. Return to hotel for a traditional Khmer herbal massage at the hotel spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private cultural performance — arrange a private Apsara dance performance (classical Khmer court dance, UNESCO-listed) at a heritage venue or your hotel's courtyard. Follow with dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast buffet — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian rice porridge, eggs Benedict, pastries, and premium Cambodian single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet picnic lunch enjoyed in a shaded temple pavilion — sandwiches, fresh fruit, sparkling water, and local snacks
meals.dinner: Private Apsara dinner experience — set Khmer menu with grilled river fish, stir-fried morning glory, and banana blossom salad, served during the performance

day_by_day.notes: Book the Apsara performance in advance. The hotel spa should be reserved the evening before. November weather is ideal — dry season beginning, expect warm days around 28–30°C.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Beng Mealea — a remote, largely unrestored 12th-century temple 40 km east of Siem Reap, often called the 'jungle temple.' Arrive early before day-trippers. Private vehicle with guide. The site feels genuinely adventurous with collapsed galleries and trees growing through stone.
day_by_day.afternoon: En route back, stop at the floating villages of Kompong Khleang on Tonlé Sap Lake — a more authentic and less-visited alternative to Chong Kneas. Private boat tour of the stilted village community. Witness daily lake life and the extraordinary biodiversity of Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in town (Asana Wooden House or equivalent). Explore the Siem Reap night market area for artisan crafts and silk goods. Dinner at a premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Local riverside restaurant near Kompong Khleang — fresh lake fish grilled with lemongrass, steamed rice, and local vegetables
meals.dinner: Embassy Restaurant or Malis Siem Reap — refined Cambodian cuisine; try the Khmer black pepper crab and lotus stem salad

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 07:30 to reach Beng Mealea early. The road to Beng Mealea is paved and comfortable in a private vehicle. Bring sturdy footwear for temple exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter or scenic flight transfer from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 45 minutes by helicopter or 1 hour by domestic flight). Check in to a luxury Phnom Penh hotel (Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal). Morning visit to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the gilded spires and emerald Buddha are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia — the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture, including masterpieces from Angkor. Private guided tour with a museum scholar. Afternoon stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade. Optional: visit to the Central Market (Psar Thmei) for luxury Cambodian silk and gemstones.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence aboard a private chartered boat. Champagne and canapés on deck as the city glitters at dusk. Dinner at a top Phnom Penh restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Siem Reap before transfer
meals.lunch: Rooftop lunch at Vann Restaurant or equivalent in Phnom Penh — panoramic Mekong views, Cambodian-French fusion cuisine
meals.dinner: Topaz Restaurant or Khéma Pasteur — French-Cambodian fine dining; foie gras, Kampot pepper steak, and crème brûlée with Cambodian palm sugar

day_by_day.notes: Book helicopter transfer well in advance. Confirm Phnom Penh hotel check-in time. Royal Palace is closed on Monday mornings — verify opening hours.

day_by_day.morning: Sobering but essential cultural visit to the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Memorial (Killing Fields) — deeply important for understanding Cambodia's recent history. Private guide provides thoughtful, respectful context. Allow 3–4 hours for both sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a restorative spa treatment — the emotional weight of the morning warrants quiet reflection. Afternoon visit to Wat Phnom, the hilltop temple that gave Phnom Penh its name. Explore the French colonial architecture of the surrounding boulevards by private tuk-tuk.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the vibrant BKK1 district for boutique shopping — Cambodian silk scarves, artisan jewelry, and contemporary Khmer art. Dinner at a celebrated Phnom Penh fine dining establishment.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a French-style café in BKK1 — croque monsieur, fresh salads, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.dinner: Malis Phnom Penh — flagship of Cambodian haute cuisine; chef's tasting menu featuring rare Cambodian ingredients like kroeung paste, wild honey, and Kampot pepper

day_by_day.notes: The Killing Fields and S-21 are emotionally intense. Schedule the spa immediately after returning. Dress modestly for temple and museum visits.

day_by_day.morning: Private vehicle transfer from Phnom Penh to Kep (approximately 3 hours) via the scenic coastal road. Stop en route at Kampot — a charming French colonial riverside town. Visit a Kampot pepper plantation for a private tasting tour — Kampot pepper is among the world's finest and holds a UNESCO Geographical Indication.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Kep — Cambodia's elegant former French colonial beach retreat. Check in to a luxury boutique property (Knai Bang Chatt or equivalent). Explore Kep National Park: hike through jungle trails to hilltop viewpoints overlooking the Gulf of Thailand. Visit the iconic Kep Crab Market — a must.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on your private villa terrace or the hotel's clifftop bar overlooking the Gulf of Thailand. The coastline at dusk is spectacular. Seafood dinner at the hotel or waterfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phnom Penh before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kampot at Rikitikitavi or equivalent — riverside setting, fresh Cambodian dishes with Kampot pepper
meals.dinner: Kep crab cooked in Kampot pepper sauce at the hotel's beachfront restaurant — the definitive Cambodian coastal dish

day_by_day.notes: The Kampot pepper farm visit should be pre-arranged. Kep is small and quiet — perfect for relaxation. November is the start of dry season; expect calm seas and pleasant evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter from Kep to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a 20-minute crossing to a pristine, largely undeveloped island with white sand beaches and turquoise water. Morning swimming, snorkeling in the coral reefs, and beach relaxation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Kep. Afternoon at leisure — hotel pool, beach, or a traditional Khmer massage at the hotel spa. Optional: kayaking along the Kep coastline or cycling through the quiet coastal roads past abandoned French colonial villas.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset fishing trip with a local fisherman — cast nets in the traditional style and watch the sun sink into the Gulf of Thailand. Return for dinner at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before boat departure
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood barbecue on Rabbit Island beach — grilled fish, prawns, and squid caught that morning, served with rice and local sauces
meals.dinner: Hotel fine dining — multi-course seafood tasting menu; lobster thermidor, Kep crab bisque, and tropical fruit sorbet

day_by_day.notes: Bring high-SPF sunscreen and a hat for the island day. Snorkeling equipment can be rented or brought from the hotel. The sunset fishing experience should be arranged through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Kep — final swim, spa treatment, or a sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged by the hotel. Check out and private vehicle transfer to Sihanoukville (approximately 2.5 hours) or fly directly to Sihanoukville if preferred. Board a private speedboat to Koh Rong Sanloem island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to a luxury overwater or beachfront villa on Koh Rong Sanloem (Shinta Mani Wild equivalent or Song Saa Private Island if budget allows). Afternoon beach exploration — the island's Saracen Bay offers crystalline water and powdery white sand. Snorkeling, paddleboarding, or simply unwinding.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent plankton night swim — Koh Rong Sanloem is one of the world's best locations for this magical natural phenomenon. The water glows electric blue as you move through it. Return for a romantic beachfront dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Kep
meals.lunch: Light lunch aboard the speedboat transfer or upon arrival at the island resort
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner on the sand — torches, white linen, and a bespoke menu of grilled seafood, coconut curries, and Cambodian desserts

day_by_day.notes: Song Saa Private Island is ultra-luxury and must be booked months in advance. The bioluminescent swim is best on moonless nights — check the lunar calendar. Speedboat transfer from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Sanloem takes approximately 45 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the island — sunrise beach walk, a last swim in the turquoise Gulf of Thailand, and a leisurely breakfast. Checkout and private speedboat transfer back to Sihanoukville. Domestic flight or private transfer back to Phnom Penh or Siem Reap for international departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: if time allows, a final stop for luxury souvenir shopping — Cambodian silk, Kampot pepper gift sets, artisan silver jewelry, and contemporary Khmer art make exceptional keepsakes. Airport lounge access arranged.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Farewell to Cambodia with memories of ancient temples, vibrant culture, and pristine tropical coastline.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast — tropical fruit, fresh pastries, eggs to order, and Cambodian coffee on the beach terrace
meals.lunch: Airport or transit lunch — premium lounge dining or a final Cambodian meal at a restaurant near the departure airport
meals.dinner: In-flight or post-departure depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and allow ample transfer time from the island. Speedboat + airport transfer can take 2.5–3 hours total — plan accordingly. Tip guides and hotel staff generously as a final gesture.
